draft.title: Spotting and avoiding scams
card: Scams have warning signs. One is pressure to act fast, such as "pay in the next hour or lose your chance".
Another is a request for gift cards or personal details, such as a password or a code sent to your phone. Real businesses do not ask for these.
A deal that looks too good to be true, such as a brand new phone for a tiny price, is also a warning sign.
If you are unsure, check with Scamwatch, the Australian Government's scam website. Never share your passwords or codes with anyone.
draft.remember: Pressure, odd payment or detail requests and deals too good to be true are warning signs. Check, and never share codes.

a.q: Which message shows a warning sign of a scam?
opts: Send gift card codes in the next hour to keep your account
Your parcel is out for delivery and will arrive tomorrow
Your school library book is due back next Friday
Your phone plan bill is ready to view in your account
a.why: Asking for gift card codes and demanding quick action are both warning signs. The other messages give ordinary information and ask for nothing risky.
a.clue: Look for pressure and an unusual way to pay.

b.q: Priya gets a text with a code from her email provider. Then a caller says he is from the provider and asks her to read the code out. What should she do?
opts: Hang up, keep the code private and check with Scamwatch
Read out the code, because he knows her email provider
Read out only half of the code to be safe
Ask him to send the request in writing, then read it out
b.why: Codes must never be shared, even with someone who sounds official. Knowing the provider's name does not prove he is real, and sharing even part of a code is still risky.
b.clue: Should a code ever be read out to someone else?

a.best: Send gift card codes in the next hour to keep your account

problems.detail: "Real businesses do not ask for these" follows "gift cards or personal details", so it reads as if real businesses never ask for any personal details. Real businesses often ask for a name, address or date of birth, for example to deliver a parcel or check who you are. The line should be limited to passwords, one-time codes and payment by gift card.
